title: Finding
description: The structured output every specialist agent (Build & Test, Security) must return, one per issue found. This is the contract the Structured Output Parser in n8n validates against. category must match a key in config/scoring.json so the scorer can look up its deduction/cap/gate.

id.description: Unique within one run, assigned by the agent (F-1, F-2, ...)

category.description: Must match a category key in config/scoring.json

title.description: One-line, human-readable. Shown as the headline in the report.

classification.description: Free-text label the agent chose within its category (e.g. 'flaky', 'regression', 'reachable', 'unreachable'). Kept separate from category so the report can show the agent's own words.

confidence.description: PRD 6.1: low confidence on a finding with a high-weight category (see scoring.json manual_review_categories) forces the run into MANUAL_REVIEW regardless of score.

source_tool.description: Which tool call produced this evidence -- used by the validation layer to drop any evidence URL that did NOT come from an actual tool result, so the model can't fabricate links.

evidence.description: At least one evidence item is required -- a finding with zero evidence should not exist; that's what confidence:low + no tool result should produce instead (see prompts/*.md 'never guess without a tool result').

files.description: Repo-relative file paths this finding concerns. Used by the Release Manager's correlation step to link findings that touch the same file.

suspect_commit.description: Build & Test Agent only, for new_regression: the sha it believes introduced the failure, from compare_commits.

reasoning.description: One paragraph, plain language, citing which tool results led to this classification. This is what renders in the agent investigation timeline.

changed_in_pr.description: Security Agent: whether `files` overlaps the PR's changed files. Context only -- per the PRD Q2 answer, reachability itself is NOT limited to changed files (that was the false-negative bug in the original PRD; see autorelease-ai/README.md 'Deviations from the PRD').
